PullRequest.Title: Center full-width characters in two monospace cells
PullRequest.Body:
Fixes #155588.

## Summary

This PR adds the opt-in editor.forceFullwidthCharacterWidth setting for monospace fonts. When enabled, characters recognized by strings.isFullWidthCharacter are centered within exactly two monospace character cells, improving alignment for CJK and other full-width characters whose natural glyph advance does not match the editor’s cell grid.

The two-cell width model is applied consistently across:

- DOM rendering
- Cursor and caret positioning
- Mouse hit testing and selections
- Simple and advanced line wrapping
- GPU rendering fallback for affected lines
- Injected text, multiline ghost text, diff deleted-code view zones, and sticky scroll
- The setting is disabled by default and only takes effect when the configured font is detected as monospace. Basic ASCII, non-full-width characters, proportional fonts, and RTL rendering retain their existing behavior. The implementation operates on individually classified code points; multi-codepoint full-width grapheme clusters are not treated as a single unit.

## Known tradeoffs

- This behavior is opt-in and only applies when the configured editor font is detected as monospace. Proportional fonts retain their existing rendering.
- Full-width detection uses VS Code’s existing strings.isFullWidthCharacter classification rather than the complete Unicode East Asian Width specification. Supplementary-plane characters, emoji, and other characters outside those ranges are not affected.
- Classification is performed per code point represented by the renderer, not per grapheme cluster. Combining marks and other multi-codepoint sequences are handled independently and may not be centered as a single visual glyph.
- The GPU renderer do not currently apply the required per-character centering. Lines containing affected full-width characters therefore fall back to DOM rendering; other lines can continue using GPU acceleration.
- Each affected character is rendered in its own inline-block span. CJK-heavy lines consequently create more DOM elements than the standard renderer.
- Text parts containing RTL content retain their existing bidi-isolated rendering and do not receive the full-width centering treatment.

## Manual verification checklist

### 1. The core claim

- [x] Each classified full-width glyph is *centered* in its two cells — even space on either side, not left-aligned with a gap on the right.
- [x] Toggling the setting in the Settings UI updates open editors live, with no reload and no stale or torn rendering.

### 2. Cursor placement

- [x] Arrow right through `|漢字漢字|` one character at a time — the caret lands on a cell boundary each time and never inside a glyph.
- [x] Arrow left back through the same run — positions are identical to the rightward pass.
- [x] Caret sits correctly at a boundary between a full-width and a narrow character (`漢a`, `a漢`).
- [x] The caret does **not** drift progressively further off as you move right along a long CJK line.

### 3. Selection

- [x] Drag-select across a CJK run — the highlight is one continuous block, with no slivers or gaps between adjacent characters.
- [x] `Shift`+arrow through a CJK run — the selection grows one full cell-pair at a time.

### 4. Mouse hit-testing

- [x] Click the **left half** of a full-width character → caret goes before it.
- [x] Click the **right half** → caret goes after it.
- [x] Click past the end of a CJK line → caret goes to end-of-line.

### 5. Features layered on the same lines

- [x] `editor.renderWhitespace: "all"` with spaces adjacent to CJK — the middot renders at its normal position, with no extra gaps.
- [x] Find/replace: search for a CJK substring — match highlights align with the glyphs.
- [x] A syntax error squiggle under CJK text follows the aligned glyphs.
- [x] A hover popup anchored to a CJK token appears in the right place.

### 6. Fonts, size, zoom

- [x] Proportional font (`"editor.fontFamily": "Georgia"`) → the setting has no effect because `effectiveForceFullwidthCharacterWidth` computes to `false`.
- [x] Changing `editor.fontSize` → box width follows.
- [x] `Ctrl`/`Cmd`+`=` editor zoom in and out → alignment holds.
- [x] `editor.letterSpacing` set to a non-zero value (try `1.5` and `3`) → alignment still holds.

Findings.ConfidenceRationale: The per-character span is explicit in the changed loop, and the complete synchronous call path is established: _constructLines queues every model line, finalize builds one HTML string/container, assigns innerHTML, appends it to document.body, and reads layout before returning. The only magnitude uncertainty is how often users combine the opt-in width mode with advanced wrapping and very large CJK files; advanced wrapping is also selected automatically with accessibility support.
Findings.PerformanceResource: temporary DOM nodes, HTML bytes, style/layout work, and Range geometry reads
Findings.PerformanceScaling: Cost and peak retained DOM grow linearly with the total number of full-width characters in the entire model, not with the viewport; all lines are placed into one container and processed serially in one finalize call.
Findings.PerformanceOutcome: blocked critical path and severe CPU/GC pressure during synchronous wrapping
Findings.PreviousBehavior: Advanced wrapping still measured the whole model synchronously, but ordinary full-width text stayed inside shared spans, normally yielding about one child span per model line rather than one per character.
Findings.ChangedBehavior: Advanced wrapping now materializes each full-width character as its own styled DOM element whenever the new two-cell option is active, instead of keeping ordinary text in large shared spans.
Findings.CausalDiffEvidence: The added full-width branch at src/vs/editor/browser/view/domLineBreaksComputer.ts:280 emits a separate inline-block span for every classified full-width character and closes it immediately after that character. Before this hunk, those characters remained in the normal shared span, which was split only at fixed-width injections or the 16,384-character safety interval.
Findings.Title: Bound the per-character advanced-wrap measurement DOM
Findings.Impact: Opening, reconfiguring, resizing/re-wrapping, or flushing a large CJK-heavy editor with `fullwidthCharacterWidth: 'twoCells'` and advanced wrapping can block the UI while the browser parses, styles, lays out, and measures hundreds of thousands of temporary elements; peak DOM memory and GC pressure grow at the same time.
Findings.Evidence: ViewModelLinesFromProjectedModel._constructLines queues all model lines and calls finalize synchronously (viewModelLines.ts:125-139). DOMLineBreaksComputer.createLineBreaks renders all queued lines into one StringBuilder, assigns the result to one container's innerHTML, appends that container to document.body, and synchronously calls Range.getClientRects while discovering breaks (domLineBreaksComputer.ts:75-195, 386-438). The changed branch at lines 273-297 creates and closes an inline-block span around every full-width code unit. Thus a 200k-character CJK model produces roughly 200k child spans in one temporary live DOM subtree, whereas the previous path generally used one span per line (with only 16,384-character splits).
Findings.Recommendation: Keep measurement semantics but bound the fan-out: process queued lines/characters in capped batches so only a limited temporary subtree is live at once, and where possible compute fixed two-cell runs outside the browser instead of emitting one measurement element per character.

Scenarios.Scenario: Open or rewrap a large CJK-heavy editor using two-cell character width and advanced wrapping.
Scenarios.CriticalPath: Editor construction, a wrapping-affecting configuration change, model flush, or advanced rewrap synchronously completes HTML generation, innerHTML parsing, DOM attachment, style/layout, and Range geometry reads before the view model can finish and render.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Serialize all lines to HTML, materialize a live measurement DOM subtree, and synchronously read browser geometry.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One temporary element per full-width character across all queued model lines after the diff; realistic CJK-heavy models can produce hundreds of thousands of elements in one subtree, followed by multiple Range.getClientRects reads per wrapped line.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The same advanced-wrap DOM boundary existed, but ordinary full-width text was grouped in shared spans (normally one child span per line, split only around injections or every 16,384 characters) rather than one child per character.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: DOM parsing, attachment, layout, and geometry measurement must finish synchronously before line projections and editor layout can proceed.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: Total classified full-width characters in the entire model, with no viewport reduction, grouping, cache hit, or batching on full reconstruction.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: All model lines and their geometry reads execute serially on the UI thread in one finalize call; there is no chunking, yielding, queue, or backpressure.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: No viewport or line-break cache bounds the configuration/open path: construction queues every model line into one finalize call. Incremental edits request only changed/inserted lines, but changing font/wrapping/two-cell policy reconstructs all projections.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: Very high: the added loop emits and closes one span per classified character, while _constructLines demonstrably queues every model line into the one live measurement container.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: The exact affected population depends on users enabling the new two-cell option and selecting advanced wrapping; accessibility mode selects advanced automatically. Browser-specific duration is unmeasured, but whole-model cardinality and synchronous reachability are explicit.
Scenarios.Verdict: Reportable high-severity regression: the PR materially amplifies an already slow synchronous boundary from roughly line-scaled DOM children to character-scaled children and peak live DOM.

Scenarios.Scenario: Type, scroll, and render dense CJK text with two-cell mode enabled.
Scenarios.CriticalPath: For changed or newly visible lines, token splitting and HTML serialization occur before DOM line rendering; browser layout is subsequently needed for widths and caret/range geometry.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Split line parts around every full-width character and serialize each as a fixed-width inline-block span.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One rendered span per classified full-width character in visible/changed text, plus one character-classification pass; bounded to rendered lines and the configured per-line render cap.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: Full-width characters shared syntax/decorations spans; DOM cardinality tracked token/decorations parts rather than characters.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Adds HTML bytes, DOM nodes, and style/layout work before the frame completes.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: Classified full-width characters among visible or changed rendered lines, after the 10,000-character line cap.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: Visible line rendering is synchronous and serial on the UI thread, but cardinality is viewport-bounded and long-line output is capped by stopRenderingLineAfter (10,000 by default).
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: ViewLine input equality avoids rebuilding unchanged visible lines, and pixel offsets are cached per rendered line where the existing cache is enabled. Scrolling or edits still render newly visible/changed lines.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High for added allocation and DOM fan-out; lower that it independently causes a user-visible regression at normal viewport sizes.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Dense CJK viewports can create thousands of nodes, but viewport bounds and the opt-in setting make this less severe than the whole-model advanced-wrap path, and individual boxes implement the requested centering semantics.
Scenarios.Verdict: No separate finding: this is the direct visible rendering implementation, is viewport/cap bounded, and evidence does not establish an independent high-confidence regression beyond the reported unbounded whole-model measurement path.

Scenarios.Scenario: Render CJK text with experimental GPU acceleration and two-cell mode enabled.
Scenarios.CriticalPath: Each visible line must pass eligibility before GPU buffer population. Lines containing a classified full-width character fall back to the existing DOM renderer so the requested two-cell styling can be applied.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Scan rendered content for full-width characters and reject GPU rendering when specialized DOM boxes are required.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: At most one bounded content scan per visible line per GPU render pass; lines with full-width content are routed to one DOM line render rather than duplicated across GPU and DOM.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: Eligible CJK lines could remain on the GPU path; no specialized content scan was performed.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: The scan is on the frame path, and fallback lines incur DOM rendering, but both are viewport-bounded.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: Visible line count times rendered content length, capped per line; effective fallback count is only lines containing classified full-width characters.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: Eligibility checks and GPU/DOM routing are serial per visible line on the render thread; no external concurrency or queue is involved.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: GPU eligibility is recomputed per visible line during rendering. There is no memoized full-width-presence flag, but scanning is limited by stopRenderingLineAfter; unchanged full-file GPU lines may later be skipped only after eligibility is checked.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High for the scan and fallback routing; uncertain that the bounded extra scan alone is material.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: GPU usage and CJK density vary, and the option documentation explicitly warns of rendering cost. No measured frame regression or avoidable semantics-preserving GPU implementation is established.
Scenarios.Verdict: No finding: fallback is required by the feature's unsupported GPU representation and remains viewport-bounded; the avoidable scan overhead is not proven material.

Scenarios.Scenario: Move or reveal the caret and render selections adjacent to a two-cell full-width character.
Scenarios.CriticalPath: Caret placement, reveals, and collapsed selection geometry may synchronously query an element box; this replaces the existing collapsed Range geometry query for those positions rather than adding a second successful layout read.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Read the fixed-width child element's client rect to obtain its cell edge.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One getClientRects call for an uncached queried position adjacent to a full-width character; fallback to the old Range read only if the element lookup/read returns no usable rect.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The same scenario synchronously read a collapsed DOM Range's client rect to locate the glyph edge.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Geometry is needed before caret/range placement can complete, as was already true for non-basic text.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: Uncached caret/range positions queried near full-width characters, generally one position per caret/reveal operation.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: Geometry reads are serial on the UI thread and occur per uncached requested position; there is no IPC, filesystem, network, or subprocess work.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: RenderedViewLine caches pixel offsets per column when its existing cache is active; cache lifetime is the rendered line. The new branch runs only next to a classified full-width character.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High that the changed read is critical-path geometry; high that it substitutes for an existing layout read rather than introducing repeated layout.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Browser costs of element versus Range rect reads may differ, but call cardinality does not increase on the successful path and cached offsets prevent repeated reads.
Scenarios.Verdict: No finding: the changed geometry operation replaces an already-required synchronous geometry read and is cached under the same lifecycle.

Analysis.Summary: Completed the performance pass over all 24 changed files and every diff hunk. Traced editor construction/configuration, advanced whole-model wrapping, visible DOM rendering, GPU eligibility/fallback, and caret geometry. Submitted one high-confidence whole-model DOM fan-out finding; no subprocess, IPC, filesystem, database, or network boundaries are reached by these paths.
